name: RotatingText-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The complete sentence is settled with its longest keyword in blue.

tagline: One word in a sentence swaps out for another every couple of seconds.
summary: A fixed sentence keeps one slot open for a changing word: each phrase slides up from below as the last slides out. The swapping word sits in bright blue against the white rest.
appearance: A short sentence in bold white type sits centred on black, with one word picked out in bright blue. The line is compact and tightly spaced.
behaviour: Every couple of seconds the blue word drops away and the next rises from below the baseline, leaving a short gap in the middle of the sentence. The words on either side never move.
demo_content: Reads "We build beautiful apps.", cycling beautiful, fast, accessible and modern.
use_when: A headline should name several qualities, audiences or verbs in the same slot.
avoid_when: Screens that need constant reading: the keyword vanishes during each swap, as frames 3 and 5 show.
customise: The phrase list, interval, split mode, stagger, spring transition, loop and autoplay are props; colours and spacing come from class overrides.
weight_why: A few animated character spans swapped on a timer.

a11y.note: The current word is mirrored for screen readers, but swaps ignore reduced-motion and there are no visible controls.

issues: Frames 3 and 5 show an empty gap where the keyword has left and the next has not arrived.
polish_why: Clean inline type and a springy swap; the blank gap between words breaks the line oddly.
